conditions.name: Asthma
conditions.overview: Study persistent-asthma controller choices using the US NAEPP focused update; this module does not cover every asthma severity or acute emergency.

sources.title: 2020 Focused Updates to the Asthma Management Guidelines: Clinician’s Guide
sources.organization: NHLBI / National Asthma Education and Prevention Program
sources.edition: 2020 focused update; clinician guide PDF revised February 2021
sources.locator: Pages 3–5: ages 4+, SMART, and long-acting muscarinic antagonists

sections.title: Controller and reliever
sections.text: For moderate-to-severe persistent asthma in people aged at least four years, NAEPP recommends ICS-formoterol as both maintenance and relief therapy.

sections.title: SMART boundaries
sections.text: The SMART evidence concerns formoterol. ICS-salmeterol maintenance should not be paired with ICS-formoterol as its reliever.

sections.title: Add-on treatment
sections.text: When ICS alone is insufficient, adding a LABA is preferred to adding a LAMA; a LAMA is an alternative when LABA cannot be used.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old has moderate persistent asthma despite an appropriate low-dose ICS regimen. Adherence and inhaler technique are confirmed. Which guideline-preferred regimen uses one inhaler for maintenance and symptom relief?
questions.explanation: NAEPP recommends ICS-formoterol maintenance-and-reliever therapy in this setting.

distractorExplanations.A: No infection is described.
distractorExplanations.B: This lacks the recommended ICS-containing SMART regimen.
distractorExplanations.C: LAMA alone does not provide the recommended controller combination.
distractorExplanations.D: This is not the preferred step-up strategy.

questions.learningObjective: Select the ICS-formoterol SMART approach.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old with persistent asthma remains symptomatic on ICS alone. Technique and adherence are adequate. A LABA is available and tolerated. Which add-on is preferred by the US focused guideline?

choices.text: Add a LABA to the ICS
Add a LAMA instead of any LABA

questions.explanation: The focused update favors LABA addition over LAMA addition when LABA can be used.

distractorExplanations.A: Antibiotics are not the specified controller step.
distractorExplanations.C: The recommended add-on retains ICS.
distractorExplanations.D: This removes the existing controller.
distractorExplanations.E: LAMA is the alternative when LABA cannot be used.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish preferred LABA addition from the LAMA alternative.

conditions.name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
conditions.overview: Study confirmation, risk reduction and symptomatic maintenance treatment using the newly posted US VA/DoD 2026 guideline.

sources.title: VA/DOD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease – Provider Summary
sources.organization: US Department of Veterans Affairs / Department of Defense
sources.edition: September 2026; official file posted October 7, 2026

sections.title: Diagnostic confirmation
sections.text: VA/DoD suggests post-bronchodilator spirometry to confirm a clinical COPD diagnosis.

sections.title: Risk reduction
sections.text: Smoking cessation with complete abstinence is recommended. Respiratory vaccination is also suggested to reduce exacerbation risk.

sections.title: Maintenance selection
sections.text: For significant symptom burden, LABA/LAMA combination is recommended over monotherapy. Prior-year exacerbations requiring steroids or antibiotics support ICS/LABA/LAMA triple therapy.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old smoker has progressive exertional dyspnea and chronic cough. COPD is suspected clinically. Which test best follows the VA/DoD confirmation recommendation?
questions.explanation: Post-bronchodilator spirometry confirms the clinical diagnosis.

distractorExplanations.B: Imaging alone does not replace spirometric confirmation.
distractorExplanations.C: A treatment response does not confirm COPD.
distractorExplanations.D: This does not confirm COPD.
distractorExplanations.E: This does not establish chronic airflow obstruction.

questions.learningObjective: Choose objective COPD confirmation.

questions.stem: A patient with confirmed COPD has significant daily symptom burden despite bronchodilator monotherapy. Which maintenance change is specifically recommended over monotherapy in the 2026 VA/DoD guideline?
questions.explanation: The 2026 guideline recommends LABA/LAMA over monotherapy for significant symptom burden.

distractorExplanations.A: This removes symptomatic treatment.
distractorExplanations.B: This is not dual bronchodilation.
distractorExplanations.D: This is not the recommended maintenance escalation.
distractorExplanations.E: This is not the specified bronchodilator escalation.

questions.learningObjective: Apply dual long-acting bronchodilation for significant COPD symptoms.

conditions.name: Community-acquired pneumonia
conditions.overview: Study adult CAP recognition, severity and inpatient regimen selection. Updated disputed viral-positive and duration questions are outside this module.

sources.title: CAP Clinical Pathway
sources.organization: Infectious Diseases Society of America
sources.edition: Official pathway based on 2019 ATS/IDSA guideline; posted version date not stated in PDF

sections.title: Recognition
sections.text: Adult CAP assessment combines a new imaging infiltrate with respiratory symptoms and another compatible clinical finding.

sections.title: Severe disease
sections.text: Vasopressor-dependent septic shock or respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation is a major severe-CAP criterion.

sections.title: Nonsevere inpatient treatment
sections.text: Without MRSA or Pseudomonas risk factors, a beta-lactam plus macrolide is a preferred inpatient regimen; a respiratory fluoroquinolone is another pathway option.

questions.stem: An immunocompetent adult with imaging-confirmed CAP requires mechanical ventilation for respiratory failure. How should the severity be classified under the IDSA pathway?

choices.text: Mild CAP because only one criterion exists

questions.explanation: Mechanical ventilation is a major criterion; one major criterion establishes severe CAP.

distractorExplanations.A: Ventilatory support excludes this description.
distractorExplanations.C: The case has imaging-confirmed pneumonia.
distractorExplanations.D: A major criterion is sufficient.
distractorExplanations.E: This is active acute illness.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize a major severe-CAP criterion.

questions.stem: An adult is hospitalized with nonsevere CAP and has no MRSA or Pseudomonas risk factors, medication allergies or relevant contraindications. Which pair matches the pathway’s preferred regimen class?
questions.explanation: The preferred pair is a beta-lactam with a macrolide.

distractorExplanations.A: No resistant-pathogen indication is provided.
distractorExplanations.C: This omits the described antibacterial regimen.
distractorExplanations.D: These are not antibacterial classes.
distractorExplanations.E: This is not the recommended pair.

questions.learningObjective: Select standard nonsevere inpatient CAP antibacterial classes.

conditions.name: Acute uncomplicated bronchitis
conditions.overview: Study uncomplicated adult cough after pneumonia has been considered.

sources.title: Outpatient Clinical Care for Adults
sources.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.edition: Current official web page; edition not stated

sections.title: Assessment
sections.text: Assess vitals and lungs for pneumonia.

sections.title: Sputum interpretation
sections.text: Sputum color does not prove bacterial infection.

sections.title: Antibiotic stewardship
sections.text: No routine antibiotics, irrespective of cough duration.

questions.stem: A healthy adult has a cough with green sputum, normal vital signs and no focal lung findings. Uncomplicated bronchitis is diagnosed. Which action best fits CDC guidance?
questions.explanation: Color does not justify antibiotics.

distractorExplanations.A: Not routine.
distractorExplanations.B: Color doesn't establish bacteria.
distractorExplanations.D: Duration doesn't justify antibiotics.
distractorExplanations.E: No severe illness.

questions.learningObjective: Avoid color-driven antibiotic prescribing.

questions.stem: An adult labeled as having bronchitis now has tachypnea and focal consolidation on examination. What should be reassessed first?
questions.explanation: Reassess for pneumonia.

distractorExplanations.A: Misses pneumonia.
distractorExplanations.B: Misses pneumonia.
distractorExplanations.C: Misses pneumonia.
distractorExplanations.E: Color isn't diagnostic.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize when the uncomplicated-bronchitis pathway no longer applies.

conditions.name: Acute bacterial rhinosinusitis
conditions.overview: Study adult bacterial sinusitis patterns and uncomplicated management.

sources.title: Outpatient Clinical Care for Adults
sources.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.edition: Current official web page; edition not stated

sections.title: Bacterial patterns
sections.text: Bacterial clues: >10 days unimproved, severe illness, or deterioration after improvement.

sections.title: Observation
sections.text: Uncomplicated: watchful waiting with reliable follow-up.

sections.title: Antibiotic selection
sections.text: First-line antibiotics: amoxicillin/amoxicillin-clavulanate; avoid azithromycin because of resistance.

questions.stem: An adult improves after a respiratory illness, then develops renewed fever, facial discomfort and increased nasal discharge. Which pattern supports bacterial sinusitis?
questions.explanation: Improvement followed by worsening.

distractorExplanations.B: Symptoms worsened.
distractorExplanations.C: No worsening.
distractorExplanations.D: Not double worsening.
distractorExplanations.E: No worsening.

questions.learningObjective: Identify double worsening.

questions.stem: An uncomplicated adult case has reliable follow-up and no urgent complication. Which non-antibiotic initial approach is supported?
questions.explanation: Uncomplicated, reliable follow-up: observe.

distractorExplanations.A: No complication.
distractorExplanations.B: Not observation.
distractorExplanations.D: Not routine.
distractorExplanations.E: No indication.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize observation as a valid option.

conditions.name: Group A streptococcal pharyngitis
conditions.overview: Study confirmation, age-specific negative-test follow-up and treatment of confirmed GAS pharyngitis.

sources.title: Clinical Guidance for Group A Streptococcal Pharyngitis
sources.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.edition: Current official web page; edition not stated

sections.title: Testing indications
sections.text: Clear viral features obviate GAS testing. Without such features, examination alone cannot reliably distinguish GAS from viral pharyngitis.

sections.title: Negative rapid test
sections.text: A symptomatic child aged at least three years needs a throat culture after a negative RADT; adults do not routinely need that backup.

sections.title: Confirmed infection
sections.text: A positive RADT or culture warrants antibiotics. Penicillin or amoxicillin is preferred when appropriate.

questions.stem: An eight-year-old has abrupt sore throat and fever without cough or rhinorrhea. The RADT is negative. What is the appropriate next diagnostic step?

choices.text: No further testing in any child
Serum antistreptolysin O to diagnose this episode

questions.explanation: Symptomatic children in this age group need culture backup after negative RADT.

distractorExplanations.A: This applies neither to the age nor CDC pathway.
distractorExplanations.B: This is not the recommended acute confirmation test.
distractorExplanations.C: This does not confirm GAS.
distractorExplanations.E: Confirmation remains needed.

questions.learningObjective: Apply age-specific backup testing.

questions.stem: An otherwise healthy adult with no penicillin allergy has GAS confirmed by RADT. Which oral antibiotic is a CDC first choice?
questions.explanation: Amoxicillin or penicillin is recommended for confirmed GAS.

distractorExplanations.A: Confirmed infection warrants treatment.
distractorExplanations.C: This is not the stated first choice.
distractorExplanations.D: This is not the stated first choice.
distractorExplanations.E: This is not the stated first choice.

questions.learningObjective: Select narrow first-line treatment for confirmed GAS.

conditions.name: Influenza
conditions.overview: Study prioritization and timing of influenza antivirals, rather than assuming every case requires medication.

sources.title: Influenza Antiviral Medications: Summary for Clinicians
sources.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.edition: Current official web page; edition not stated
sources.locator: Priority Groups; Antiviral Drug Options; co-circulation

sections.title: Treatment priority
sections.text: Hospitalization, severe or progressive illness, and higher complication risk favor prompt antiviral treatment for suspected or confirmed influenza.

sections.title: Timing
sections.text: Do not delay priority-group treatment for test results. Progressive illness can warrant treatment beyond two days of symptoms.

sections.title: Hospitalized illness
sections.text: Oral or enteric oseltamivir should be started promptly in hospitalized patients with suspected or confirmed influenza.

questions.stem: A 72-year-old is hospitalized with suspected influenza pneumonia during active community transmission. Testing is pending. What is the best antiviral approach?

choices.text: Start oral or enteric oseltamivir promptly
Avoid antivirals if symptoms exceed two days
Give antibiotics as the only influenza treatment

questions.explanation: Hospitalized suspected influenza warrants prompt oseltamivir without waiting for confirmation.

distractorExplanations.B: Testing should not delay treatment here.
distractorExplanations.C: The two-day cutoff does not exclude priority treatment.
distractorExplanations.D: This delays indicated therapy.
distractorExplanations.E: Antibiotics do not replace influenza antiviral treatment.

questions.learningObjective: Prioritize empiric antiviral treatment in hospitalized suspected influenza.

questions.stem: A patient with chronic lung disease presents on day four of suspected influenza with progressively worsening illness. Which principle best fits CDC recommendations?

choices.text: All antiviral benefit ends at 48 hours
No testing or treatment is permitted
Only symptom-free contacts can receive antivirals

questions.explanation: Progressive illness supports prompt antiviral treatment even beyond two days.

distractorExplanations.B: This is an inappropriate absolute cutoff.
distractorExplanations.C: This is not the priority pathway.
distractorExplanations.D: The patient is symptomatic.
distractorExplanations.E: This unnecessarily delays care in the vignette.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish priority illness from the early uncomplicated outpatient window.

conditions.name: COVID-19
conditions.overview: Study risk-based early outpatient antiviral treatment. Eligibility, interactions and product labels require current checking.

sources.title: COVID-19 Treatment Clinical Care for Outpatients
sources.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.edition: Official page updated October 8, 2026

sections.title: Risk-based treatment
sections.text: Consider antivirals for mild-to-moderate disease with risk factors for severe outcomes; advancing age and immunocompromise are important risks.

sections.title: Oral option
sections.text: Nirmatrelvir-ritonavir must start within five days. Review eligibility and drug interactions before choosing it.

sections.title: Intravenous alternative
sections.text: A three-day remdesivir course started within seven days is a preferred alternative when nirmatrelvir-ritonavir is unsuitable.

questions.stem: A high-risk adult has mild COVID-19 on symptom day three. Nirmatrelvir-ritonavir is being considered. Which additional step is essential before selection?
questions.explanation: Ritonavir interactions and treatment eligibility must be reviewed within the treatment window.

distractorExplanations.B: Outpatient risk-based treatment does not require hypoxemia.
distractorExplanations.C: This misses the oral treatment window.
distractorExplanations.D: Antibiotics do not replace antiviral selection.
distractorExplanations.E: Interactions can determine suitability.

questions.learningObjective: Check interactions before early oral COVID-19 treatment.

questions.stem: A high-risk adult with mild COVID-19 presents on day six. Nirmatrelvir-ritonavir cannot be used, and remdesivir is accessible and appropriate. Which course fits CDC outpatient guidance?

choices.text: No antiviral option because five days elapsed

questions.explanation: Remdesivir can begin within seven days as a three-day outpatient course.

distractorExplanations.A: This exceeds the stated oral window.
distractorExplanations.B: Remdesivir has a seven-day window.
distractorExplanations.D: This is not a COVID-19 regimen.
distractorExplanations.E: This is not an antiviral regimen.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the remdesivir outpatient window.

conditions.name: Allergic rhinitis
conditions.overview: Study evidence-based nasal treatment and testing limits from the US Joint Task Force practice parameter.

sources.title: Rhinitis 2020: A practice parameter update
sources.organization: Joint Task Force on Practice Parameters / AAAAI and ACAAI
sources.edition: 2020 practice parameter
sources.locator: Summary; intranasal corticosteroids; montelukast; food allergy testing

sections.title: Persistent symptoms
sections.text: An intranasal corticosteroid is preferred monotherapy for persistent allergic rhinitis.

sections.title: Inadequate response
sections.text: Combining an intranasal corticosteroid with an intranasal antihistamine can add benefit. Montelukast is reserved for inadequate response or intolerance to alternatives.

sections.title: Testing boundary
sections.text: Routine food-allergy testing is not recommended as part of a rhinitis evaluation.

questions.stem: An adult has persistent allergic rhinitis affecting daily activities and has not yet tried nasal treatment. Which monotherapy is preferred?

choices.text: Food elimination based only on an unselected panel

questions.explanation: The practice parameter favors intranasal corticosteroid monotherapy for persistent allergic rhinitis.

distractorExplanations.A: This is not preferred nasal monotherapy.
distractorExplanations.B: Montelukast is reserved for failure or intolerance of alternatives.
distractorExplanations.C: No bacterial infection is described.
distractorExplanations.E: Routine food testing is not recommended.

questions.learningObjective: Select preferred persistent-rhinitis monotherapy.

questions.stem: A patient with allergic rhinitis asks for a broad food-allergy panel despite having no food-associated symptoms. Which approach best matches the practice parameter?

choices.text: Order the panel in every rhinitis case
Require a food panel before nasal therapy
Diagnose food allergy from sneezing alone
Avoid routine food-allergy testing for rhinitis

questions.explanation: Rhinitis alone is not an indication for routine food-allergy testing.

distractorExplanations.A: Routine panels are not recommended.
distractorExplanations.B: The panel is not a prerequisite.
distractorExplanations.C: The vignette lacks a food-allergy history.
distractorExplanations.D: This does not address the question.

questions.learningObjective: Avoid unsupported food-allergy evaluation in isolated rhinitis.

conditions.name: Tuberculosis infection and disease
conditions.overview: Study the distinction between infection and active disease, BCG-related test selection and preventive treatment.

sources.title: Clinical Overview of Latent Tuberculosis Infection
sources.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.edition: Current official web page; edition not stated

sources.title: Clinical Testing and Diagnosis for Tuberculosis
sources.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.edition: Current official web page; edition not stated

sections.title: Infection versus disease
sections.text: A positive IGRA or skin test indicates infection; evaluate for active TB before assigning latent infection or starting preventive treatment.

sections.title: BCG and testing
sections.text: A TB blood test is preferred for BCG-vaccinated people aged at least five years.

sections.title: Latent infection treatment
sections.text: CDC preferentially recommends eligible three- or four-month rifamycin-based regimens over longer isoniazid monotherapy.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old BCG-vaccinated immigrant needs testing for TB infection. Which test avoids the BCG-related limitation of skin testing and is CDC-preferred?

choices.text: Routine sputum culture in all asymptomatic people
Chest radiograph as the only infection test

questions.explanation: CDC prefers a TB blood test in BCG-vaccinated people in this age group.

distractorExplanations.A: This is not the recommended test.
distractorExplanations.B: Vaccination is not a diagnostic test.
distractorExplanations.C: This is not the preferred screening test here.
distractorExplanations.D: Imaging does not replace infection testing.

questions.learningObjective: Choose IGRA for BCG-vaccinated adults.

questions.stem: A patient has a positive IGRA and is being considered for latent-TB treatment. What must occur before preventive therapy is started?

choices.text: Assume the IGRA proves active pulmonary disease
Ignore symptoms if the IGRA is positive

questions.explanation: Active disease must be excluded before latent-infection treatment.

distractorExplanations.A: This skips a required distinction.
distractorExplanations.B: IGRA alone does not establish active disease.
distractorExplanations.C: This does not exclude active disease.
distractorExplanations.E: Symptoms remain clinically relevant.

questions.learningObjective: Separate TB infection from active disease before preventive therapy.

conditions.name: Acute otitis media
conditions.overview: Study objective pediatric AOM diagnosis and initial antibiotic choice.

sources.title: Outpatient Clinical Care for Pediatric Populations
sources.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.edition: Current official web page; edition not stated

sections.title: Diagnostic evidence
sections.text: AOM requires middle-ear effusion and compatible acute findings such as a bulging tympanic membrane; erythema alone is insufficient.

sections.title: Observation candidates
sections.text: Selected mild cases can undergo shared-decision watchful waiting, with eligibility depending on age and laterality.

sections.title: Antibiotic choice
sections.text: Amoxicillin is first-line without recent exposure. Recent amoxicillin, purulent conjunctivitis or relevant recurrent treatment failure favors amoxicillin/clavulanate.

questions.stem: A child with a respiratory infection has an erythematous tympanic membrane but no middle-ear effusion on pneumatic otoscopy. What is the best conclusion?

choices.text: AOM diagnostic criteria are not met
AOM is confirmed by redness alone
All children with redness require ceftriaxone

questions.explanation: Without middle-ear effusion, CDC says not to diagnose AOM.

distractorExplanations.A: Effusion is required.
distractorExplanations.C: Recurrent disease is not established.
distractorExplanations.D: Redness alone is insufficient.
distractorExplanations.E: The diagnostic prerequisite is absent.

questions.learningObjective: Avoid diagnosing AOM from erythema alone.

questions.stem: A child has confirmed AOM requiring antibiotics and concurrent purulent conjunctivitis. There is no beta-lactam allergy. Which oral choice fits CDC guidance?

choices.text: No antibiotic because conjunctivitis is present

questions.explanation: Purulent conjunctivitis is a reason to choose amoxicillin/clavulanate.

distractorExplanations.A: The case states antibiotics are indicated.
distractorExplanations.B: This is not the specified AOM regimen.
distractorExplanations.C: This is not routine first-line AOM treatment.
distractorExplanations.E: This is not the specified choice.

questions.learningObjective: Use conjunctivitis as a modifier of AOM antibiotic choice.

conditions.name: Acute otitis externa
conditions.overview: Study external-canal infection and escalation signs. The cited HSE guideline is Irish supplementary guidance, not a US guideline.

sources.title: Acute otitis externa guideline
sources.organization: Health Service Executive, Ireland
sources.edition: Ireland; Version 2.0 reviewed March 2026

sections.title: External-canal localization
sections.text: Tragal or pinna tenderness with ear-canal inflammation supports otitis externa.

sections.title: Local treatment
sections.text: The Irish HSE guideline uses topical antimicrobial options, with attention to tympanic-membrane integrity, analgesia and keeping the ear dry.

sections.title: Escalation signs
sections.text: Cranial nerve involvement, granulation tissue or extension of pain in a high-risk patient raises concern for necrotizing disease and warrants urgent hospital referral.

questions.stem: A swimmer has rapid-onset ear pain, a swollen erythematous ear canal and marked tragal tenderness. Which anatomic diagnosis best fits these findings?
questions.explanation: The painful tragus and inflamed canal localize the problem to the external ear.

distractorExplanations.A: This does not best localize the painful canal findings.
distractorExplanations.B: No mastoid findings are described.
distractorExplanations.C: The canal is visibly inflamed.
distractorExplanations.D: The prominent findings are in the external canal.

questions.learningObjective: Localize ear pain to the external canal.

questions.stem: An older patient with diabetes has an external-ear infection, granulation tissue and new facial weakness. Which response is appropriate under the cited supplementary guideline?

choices.text: Urgent hospital referral for possible necrotizing otitis externa
Ignore the weakness if drops were prescribed

questions.explanation: High-risk infection with cranial nerve involvement requires urgent escalation.

distractorExplanations.B: This delays evaluation of a red flag.
distractorExplanations.C: The infection and weakness are not simple allergy.
distractorExplanations.D: New weakness changes the assessment.
distractorExplanations.E: This does not address possible invasive disease.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize invasive external-ear infection red flags.

conditions.name: Gastroesophageal reflux disease
conditions.overview: Study empiric treatment versus objective investigation using AGA best-practice advice.

sources.title: Personalized approach to the evaluation and management of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)
sources.organization: American Gastroenterological Association
sources.edition: 2022 clinical practice update

sections.title: Typical symptoms
sections.text: Troublesome typical symptoms without alarm features support a four- to eight-week single-dose PPI trial, then the lowest effective dose if improved.

sections.title: Investigation
sections.text: Alarm features or inadequate response to a PPI trial warrant endoscopic investigation; additional reflux testing depends on findings.

sections.title: Isolated extraesophageal symptoms
sections.text: For isolated extraesophageal symptoms with suspected reflux, AGA favors objective testing off medication before empiric PPI treatment.

questions.stem: An adult has troublesome heartburn and regurgitation without alarm features. A cardiac explanation is not suspected. Which initial strategy fits AGA advice?

choices.text: No treatment without a positive stool test
Single-dose PPI trial for four to eight weeks

questions.explanation: A time-limited single-dose PPI trial is appropriate for typical symptoms without alarms.

distractorExplanations.A: Stool testing is not the indicated prerequisite.
distractorExplanations.B: This is not GERD treatment.
distractorExplanations.D: Duration and dose should be reassessed.
distractorExplanations.E: Invasive therapy requires further confirmation.

questions.learningObjective: Use a bounded empiric PPI trial in typical uncomplicated reflux.

questions.stem: A patient treated for presumed GERD develops progressive dysphagia and has persistent symptoms despite a PPI trial. What evaluation is favored?
questions.explanation: Alarm symptoms and inadequate response favor endoscopic investigation.

distractorExplanations.B: This is unrelated to the symptom pattern.
distractorExplanations.C: This delays appropriate investigation.
distractorExplanations.D: This bypasses alarm-feature evaluation.
distractorExplanations.E: This does not address the described alarm.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize when reflux symptoms require endoscopic evaluation.

conditions.name: Peptic ulcer disease and Helicobacter pylori infection
conditions.overview: Study H. pylori-associated ulcer disease, susceptibility-aware treatment and eradication confirmation.

sources.title: ACG Guideline Highlights: Treatment of Helicobacter pylori Infection
sources.organization: American College of Gastroenterology
sources.edition: 2024 guideline highlights; underlying guideline September 2024
sources.locator: When to test; treatment table; treatment pearls

sections.title: Testing and ulcer history
sections.text: Current or previous peptic ulcer disease is an indication to assess H. pylori when prior eradication is not established.

sections.title: Treatment selection
sections.text: Optimized bismuth quadruple treatment is recommended empirically. Avoid clarithromycin- or levofloxacin-containing regimens without demonstrated susceptibility.

sections.title: Confirming eradication
sections.text: Confirm cure at least four weeks after therapy using breath, stool-antigen or biopsy testing. Hold PPIs two weeks and antibiotics/bismuth four weeks to avoid false negatives.

questions.stem: A treatment-naive adult has confirmed H. pylori infection and no susceptibility result. Which listed option best matches the empiric ACG recommendation?

choices.text: Clarithromycin triple therapy regardless of resistance
No treatment after a positive test

questions.explanation: Optimized bismuth quadruple therapy is the recommended empiric option.

distractorExplanations.A: Acid suppression alone does not provide the regimen.
distractorExplanations.B: Susceptibility is not demonstrated.
distractorExplanations.C: Confirmed infection should be treated.
distractorExplanations.E: Susceptibility is not demonstrated.

questions.learningObjective: Choose resistance-aware empiric H. pylori treatment.

questions.stem: A patient finished H. pylori therapy six weeks ago and remains on a PPI. Which plan improves the validity of a stool-antigen test of cure?

choices.text: Test one day after restarting antibiotics
Hold the PPI for two weeks before testing
Replace the test with routine antibody titers
Use symptoms alone to prove cure

questions.explanation: The timing after therapy is adequate; the PPI should be withheld for two weeks.

distractorExplanations.A: Recent antibiotics undermine testing.
distractorExplanations.B: This increases false-negative risk.
distractorExplanations.D: This is not the specified cure test.
distractorExplanations.E: Symptoms do not establish eradication.

questions.learningObjective: Prepare properly for an H. pylori test of cure.

conditions.name: Irritable bowel syndrome
conditions.overview: Study dietary management after an IBS diagnosis has been established; this is not a complete diagnostic exclusion algorithm.

sources.title: AGA Clinical Practice Update on the Role of Diet in Irritable Bowel Syndrome: Expert Review
sources.organization: American Gastroenterological Association
sources.edition: 2022 clinical practice update
sources.locator: Best practice advice 1–3 and 5–7 in official commissioned publication abstract

sections.title: Soluble fiber
sections.text: Soluble fiber can improve global IBS symptoms.

sections.title: Low-FODMAP strategy
sections.text: A low-FODMAP intervention is a bounded restriction phase of no more than four to six weeks, followed by reintroduction and individualized maintenance.

sections.title: Patient selection
sections.text: Dietitian support aids implementation. Restrictive diets are poor choices with malnutrition risk, food insecurity or an eating disorder.

questions.stem: An adult with established IBS improves during a four-week low-FODMAP trial with a dietitian. Which next step best matches the intended strategy?

choices.text: Reintroduce foods and personalize the diet

questions.explanation: Reintroduction and personalization follow the short restriction phase.

distractorExplanations.A: The restriction phase is intentionally bounded.
distractorExplanations.B: This is not the advised sequence.
distractorExplanations.D: This is not the advised sequence.
distractorExplanations.E: This does not follow the dietary strategy.

questions.learningObjective: Use all three phases of a low-FODMAP intervention.

questions.stem: A patient with IBS has an active eating disorder and a severely restricted intake. Which initial dietary recommendation is most appropriate?

choices.text: Avoid further restrictive dieting and arrange individualized nutritional support
Begin a stricter low-FODMAP elimination immediately

questions.explanation: An eating disorder makes restrictive diet interventions a poor choice; individualized support is favored.

distractorExplanations.A: This compounds restriction.
distractorExplanations.B: This compounds restriction.
distractorExplanations.D: This compounds restriction.
distractorExplanations.E: This compounds restriction.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize contraindications to restrictive IBS dietary strategies.

conditions.name: Chronic idiopathic constipation
conditions.overview: Study adult medication choices and the 2026 evaluation pathway before labeling disease refractory.

sources.title: Pharmacological management of chronic idiopathic constipation
sources.organization: American Gastroenterological Association / American College of Gastroenterology
sources.edition: 2023 joint guideline

sources.title: Evaluation and management of refractory constipation
sources.organization: American Gastroenterological Association
sources.edition: 2026 clinical practice update
sources.locator: Best practice advice: anorectal testing, secondary causes and surgery

sections.title: Medication evidence
sections.text: The joint guideline recommends polyethylene glycol for adult CIC.

sections.title: Medication escalation

sources.organization: Infectious Diseases Society of America

sections.title: Rehydration
sections.text: Reduced-osmolarity oral rehydration solution is first-line for mild-to-moderate dehydration. Shock, severe dehydration or altered mental status warrants isotonic intravenous fluids.

sections.title: Antibiotic restraint
sections.text: Most acute watery diarrhea without recent international travel does not require empiric antibiotics. Avoid antimicrobials in STEC O157 or Shiga-toxin-2 infection.

sections.title: Nutrition
sections.text: Resume an age-appropriate usual diet during or immediately after rehydration; breastfeeding should continue.

sections.text: For nonpregnant adults with suspected acute cholecystitis, IDSA suggests abdominal ultrasound first.

sections.title: After inconclusive ultrasound
sections.text: Persistent suspicion with equivocal ultrasound supports abdominal CT, particularly when complications or alternative diagnoses need evaluation.

sections.title: Persistent uncertainty
sections.text: If ultrasound and CT remain nondiagnostic, MRI/MRCP or HIDA can be used. The guideline notes direct ultrasound-to-HIDA may suit selected high-suspicion cases.

conditions.name: Acute colonic diverticulitis

sources.title: Medical management of colonic diverticulitis
sources.organization: American Gastroenterological Association
sources.edition: 2021 clinical practice update

sections.title: Confirmation
sections.text: Consider CT for a first unconfirmed episode, severe presentation, poor improvement or immunocompromise.

sections.title: Selective antibiotic treatment
sections.text: Mild uncomplicated disease in an immunocompetent patient can use antibiotics selectively. Immunocompromise, complications or higher-risk features favor antibiotics.

sections.title: Recovery evaluation
sections.text: When colonoscopy is indicated after an episode, delay it six to eight weeks or until symptoms fully resolve, whichever is longer; alarms can justify earlier evaluation.

questions.explanation: Selected mild uncomplicated cases can be managed without routine antibiotics.

sections.text: An ultrasound-first strategy with MRI after nondiagnostic results is suggested in pregnancy. Initial MRI is also reasonable when readily available.

sections.text: Start with HCV antibody and reflex to HCV RNA when reactive; antibody alone cannot establish current infection.

sections.text: Detected RNA indicates current infection and requires evaluation and linkage to direct-acting antiviral treatment; vaccination and other preventive needs also merit assessment.

conditions.name: Hepatitis B

sections.title: Triple panel
sections.text: Initial screening uses HBsAg, anti-HBs and total anti-HBc.

sections.title: Serologic patterns
sections.text: HBsAg with total anti-HBc indicates infection; IgM anti-HBc helps distinguish acute infection. Anti-HBs without anti-HBc after documented vaccination indicates vaccine-associated immunity.

sections.title: Linkage to care
sections.text: Confirmed infection needs liver-disease evaluation, monitoring and treatment assessment. Resolved infection still carries a reactivation counseling need.

questions.stem: A vaccinated adult has negative HBsAg, negative total anti-HBc and positive anti-HBs, with a documented completed vaccine series. What is the best interpretation?

distractorExplanations.E: Resolved natural infection includes core antibody.

sections.title: Initiation
sections.text: ART is recommended for all people with HIV and should start as soon as possible after diagnosis; high CD4 count is not a reason to defer.

sections.title: Engagement and adherence
sections.text: Discuss lifelong treatment, benefits and adherence, and identify barriers to sustained care. Currently available ART is not curative.

sections.title: Transmission and suppression
sections.text: Maintained HIV RNA below 200 copies/mL with ART prevents sexual transmission.

sections.title: Nonpregnant adult treatment
sections.text: Doxycycline 100 mg orally twice daily for seven days is recommended for uncomplicated adolescent and adult infection outside pregnancy.

sections.title: Partner management
sections.text: Recent sex partners need evaluation and treatment. Abstain until the regimen is complete, symptoms resolve and partners are treated.

sections.title: Follow-up
sections.text: Retest approximately three months after treatment for reinfection. Routine four-week test of cure is not indicated in nonpregnant adherent patients without ongoing symptoms or reinfection concern.
